items.note: A tall box-and-arrow pipeline, one page high and one column wide, drawn in a presentation tool: blue rounded 'Start', a filled rectangle 'addressing missing data', a decision diamond 'How is the data related to students' performance?', two branches into 'choosing performance contributing variables and determining their coefficients' and 'determining performance index', a second diamond 'Does donation amount affect the data directly?' with a 'No' arm to an oval 'Drop' and a 'Yes' arm into 'determining investment strategy', a long feedback line up the left margin labelled 'Donation amount', an 'Accounting for time duration and geographical distribution' box, and a right-hand column of four boxes from 'Fitting the relation between performance contributing variables and donation amount' to 'Maximizing ROI and determining investment strategy'. Arrow labels carry the data names - 'All data', 'Addressed data', 'Performance indicators', 'Performance index', 'Potential performance contributing variables', 'Final results For year 1', 'Final results For year 2-5'. NO AXES, no number and no value anywhere on it. TWO FEEDBACK PATHS CROSS THE FLOW WITHOUT A JUNCTION MARK: the left-margin 'Donation amount' line runs the height of the page through the same channel as the downward arrows, and the bracket from the right-hand column re-enters 'determining investment strategy' from below, so which arrow feeds which box at the crossings can only be guessed. The 'Final results' arrows converge on a single 'Finish' oval. Caption below; cited by the sentence that ends section 1.2, 'The flow chart of the whole model is presented below in Fig 1:'.

The definitions table, printed as an EMBEDDED IMAGE rather than as type: the page carries only its heading '1.3 Detailed Definitions & Assumptions' and the sub-heading '1.3.1 Detailed Definitions:', and everything under them is a bitmap, so the whole table has no text layer and no selectable cell. Three columns - a Name column, a Definition column of full sentences and a Denotation column of mathematics - over a header row and ten body rows, from 'Donation amount' (X_j) through 'ROI of the performance index (also referred as ROI for simplicity)' (ROI_j), every row ruled on all four sides in the same full grid as Table 1. NO CAPTION AND NO NUMBER: it is the only table in the paper that is never numbered, and the one that actually carries the paper's notation. The definition text is justified inside its column, which opens wide word gaps in two cells, and the denotation of 'Performance index' is a bare Greek upsilon with no subscript while its neighbours all carry one. Because it is an image, no figure or table extractor reads a cell of it, and the paper's own notation is therefore invisible to any downstream search.

note:
Paper 99, Team 42939, a donation-strategy model for the Goodgrant Foundation built on a composite
education-performance index. Twenty-five pages, fourteen measured regions on twelve of them,
resolving into TWELVE FIGURE ROWS, TWO TABLE ROWS and ONE EXCLUSION - the pure-white raster on the
title page - with nothing unaccounted.

Seven printed tables carry no measured region and therefore no row: Table 3 (the post-LASSO
coefficients, p14), Tables 4 to 8 (the investment strategy of years 1 to 5, pp19, 21 and 22), and the
untitled institution listing that runs off the foot of the letter on p2 and continues at the head of
p3. Every one of the five yearly tables prints the same three columns (UNITID, names, ROI, donation)
against twenty institutions, and the two that share a page print with no rule between them.

The definitions table is an image. On p9 the page prints the heading "1.3 Detailed Definitions &
Assumptions", the sub-heading "1.3.1 Detailed Definitions:" and then a bitmap: three columns (Name,
Definition, Denotation) over a header row and ten body rows, every row ruled on all four sides. The
paper's entire notation - X_j, delta-X_j, Y_1j to Y_mj, F_1 to F_i, beta_1 to beta_i, ROI_1j,
fROI_1j, P_1j, ROI_j - exists inside that picture and nowhere in the text layer, and it is the only
table in the paper that is neither numbered nor captioned.

Table 2 is titled "The Top 10 Institutions in Terms of Performance Index" and prints NINE rows, from
Los Angeles County College of Nursing and Allied Health at 79.60372162 to Weill Cornell Medical
College at 78.14334106. No tenth row exists on the page or on the two pages after it. Every score is
printed to eight decimals even though the index is a weighted sum of four variables uniformized to
0 to 100, and the table carries no rank column although ranking is its only content. Both it and
Table 1 are ruled as full grids - a rule under the header, a rule between every pair of body rows and
vertical rules at both edges and between the columns - the opposite of the booktabs shape the rest of
the sample uses.

Figure 1 is the whole pipeline, one page high, drawn in a presentation tool: two decision diamonds,
a 'No' arm to a 'Drop' oval, a left-margin "Donation amount" feedback line that runs the height of the
page through the same channel as the downward arrows, a right-hand column of four boxes that re-enters
"determining investment strategy" from below, and no junction marks at any crossing.

Figures 2 and 3 are the LASSO pair, printed a page BEFORE the sentences that read them. Figure 2's
top axis carries twelve vertical rules and the tick numbers 0 1 2 3 4 5 7 9 12 13 15 20 with no label,
no unit and no name, and its six variable labels sit outside the frame at the right margin tied to
square markers on the frame edge. Figure 3's cross-validated trace is flat at about 40 from s = 0.1 to
s = 1.0 and carries no marker at the chosen shrinkage, so the "minimum with shrinkage factor between
0.4-0.8. We choose 0.6" that the next page reports is not readable on the exhibit.

Figures 4 and 5 are one picture printed twice. Both are the same diamond cloud of institutions, the
same blue GAM curve, the same grey ribbon, the same axes (0e+00 to 9e+08, 0.25 to 1.00) and the same
in-frame title "GAM estimation of PCTPELL vs Donation"; Figure 5 adds an orange segment labelled
delta-h, an orange tick and a green bracket labelled delta-x and delta-f. Figure 5 is named by no
sentence - it exists to illustrate the definition of fitted ROI that the body text states in symbols.
Both print "PCTPELL" one character per line down the left margin, and both are dominated near zero
donation by point overplotting so dense that the shape the curve is fitted to cannot be checked.

Figures 6 and 7 are the tuning-parameter curve and its piecewise approximation, drawn by a
mathematics package on a fine grid with unnamed axes, ordinate labels set inside the plot area, and
unexplained red markers on the x axis. The endpoint list the prose supplies for Figure 7 contradicts
itself: both ends are described as "The minimum of deviations of all institutions", one value is
written 2/4 where its mirror is 4/3, and the curve cannot be checked against the points that define
it. Figure 6 is cited three times on one page and Figure 7 once, which makes this sketch the most
cited exhibit in the paper.

Figure 8 is a screenshot of a mapping tool: fifteen red pins with callouts truncated by the tool
itself ("The State University of...", "Marion Military Instit..."), two collided into
"SUNY at FredoniaBoston", no scale bar, no graticule, no legend, and no magnitude on any pin. The
amounts the map cannot show are in Table 4, which has no measured region.

The appendix page prints the remaining two GAM fits, Figures 9 and 10, with no text but their
captions. The four panels of this family are not on a common scale - three run 0.00 to 1.00 on the
ordinate and the fourth runs 0 to 60 - so the four fits cannot be laid against each other. Figure 9's
confidence ribbon crosses below zero, and its ordinate label collides with the 0.50 tick.

Families: scatter 4, line 4, flowchart-or-schematic 1, map-or-plan-view 1, table-as-figure 1,
table-grid 2.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: fourteen measured regions resolve into twelve figure rows, two table rows and one exclusion, and every region is accounted for once [place.doc_order].

A measured raster can be empty: the p4 region on the title page is uniform white across the whole crop, so the census excludes it as background instead of inventing an exhibit for it [caption.numbering].

A table can be printed as an image: the definitions table on p9 has no text layer at all under its headings, so it is recorded as a table-as-figure row and no cell of the paper's own notation is machine-readable [geometry.family].

Six printed tables carry no measured region and therefore no row - Table 3's post-LASSO results and Tables 4 to 8's five years of investment strategy - and the untitled institution listing that runs off p2 onto p3 has neither caption nor region, so all seven are declared gaps in the note [table.rule_style].

Two exhibits print the same picture: Figure 4 and Figure 5 are the same diamond cloud, curve, ribbon, axes and in-frame title, and the second differs only by three annotation glyphs [geometry.family].

A caption can promise more than the table prints: 'Table 2: The Top 10 Institutions in Terms of Performance Index' has nine body rows, and the text layer of the page and the two after it holds no tenth [caption.verbatim].

A chosen parameter can be unreadable on the exhibit the paper chose it from: the cross-validation trace of Figure 3 is flat from s = 0.1 to s = 1.0, so the 'minimum between 0.4-0.8' that the prose reports cannot be located, and no marker shows the 0.6 that was taken [geometry.data_labels].

A four-panel appendix is not drawn on a common scale: Figures 4, 5 and 9 run 0.00 to 1.00 on the ordinate and Figure 10 runs 0 to 60, so the four fits it exists to compare cannot be compared [geometry.shared_axes].

Citation is thin: six figure rows and both measured tables are named by a sentence, Table 1 is not, and Figures 5, 9 and 10 are named by nothing, while Figure 6 is named three times on one page [mention.count].

tables.note: A two-column, four-row grid at the foot of the baseline-model section: a header row 'Variable | Dataset' and three body rows that name the three inputs the model uses - Performance index, Performance contributing variables, Donation amount - against where each comes from, 'Excel table', 'Excel table and pdf file' and 'Pdf file'. RULING IS A FULL GRID, not the booktabs shape: a rule above the header, a rule under the header, a rule between every pair of body rows and a rule at the foot, plus VERTICAL RULES at the left edge, between the two columns and at the right edge, all at the same 0.4 pt weight, so the table closes into a box and the three sources are separated by line rather than by white space. The caption prints ABOVE it, 'Table 1: Data Source', after the prose note 'Note: we only use data from the provided excel table and that mentioned in the pdf file.'; NO SENTENCE NAMES IT. The table is 279 pt wide against a 453 pt measure, left-offset rather than centred, and it is the only 'table' in the paper whose content is a provenance statement rather than a result.
